The only real positives of this hotel are the beautiful views and the well-equipped gym. Unfortunately, everything else was a major disappointment and far below what you would expect from a 5-star hotel. Our room was located very high up in the resort, requiring us to climb countless stairs every time we wanted to get there. It honestly felt like climbing Montmartre several times a day. The hotel offers shuttle services, but with the resort being so overcrowded, finding an available one is almost impossible. The room itself is nowhere near 5-star standard. The materials and finishes feel cheap and low quality. For a hotel claiming to be 5-star, this is simply unacceptable. The restaurant is very poorly managed. The staff are clearly overwhelmed, and around 20–30 minutes before the end of the service, many dishes are no longer replenished. For example, arriving around 8:30 PM means you often have to eat whatever is left. The food itself is bland, repetitive and of disappointing quality. The sunbed situation is also ridiculous. Guests reserve sunbeds for hours without using them, while management does nothing to control the situation. Finding an available sunbed is almost impossible. What is perhaps most disappointing is seeing the hotel staff working under such obvious pressure, in extremely hot conditions and with an overwhelming workload. You can genuinely feel sorry for them. The problem does not seem to be the employees themselves, but rather the way the hotel is managed and the lack of resources provided to them. The attitude of some managers and reception staff is also far from what you would expect from a 5-star property: little warmth, little consideration and very little willingness to help. Apart from the view and the gym, this hotel was a huge disappointment. In my opinion, it does not deserve 5 stars —honestly, not even 4. We definitely will not be coming back.
